tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_quarter_ss idealized supercell (GNU real32 build, dx = 2 km, dt = 12 s, 40 layers, WSM6 only) dumped by the instrumented ctessum-claude/WRF fork (module_esm_dump with esm_dump_inner hooks inside mp_wsm6_run of the ctessum-claude/MMM-physics fork, commit 52cfbd7) and replayed through the real64 (kind_phys = real64) standalone kernels/wsm6_driver at the WRF step. POINTWISE and step-free: the inputs are the state at which the kernel evaluates its process rates (t_rates, qi/qr/qs/qg_rates: after the sub-step's sedimentation, melting, freezing and the slope update; den: kernel argument), the expected values are the inverse slopes, their powers and n0sfac the kernel dumps for that state and the mp_wsm6_init constants, all from the real64 replay. The rates state is the correct one because slope_wsm6 is called again after melting/freezing ('update the slope parameters for microphysics computation'). Real64 replay vs real32 in-model dump: 3-4e-7 relative in rslope*. Residual esm-vs-real64 mismatch comes from the kernel's default-real literals and real32 WRF constants (pi, bvtr, bvts, avts, dens, n0s, ...; FORTRAN_BUGS.md N2): measured with zero tolerances it is <= 3e-8 relative in the inverse slopes and their powers, 1.5e-8 in the fall-speed constants; tolerances are 1e-6 relative (5-10x the measured residual) on scalars and spot checks and absolute Linf bounds at 1e-6 of each column's maximum. xni, D_i and the fall speeds are not dumped by the kernel at this state (the dumped xni is the stale value from before the ice fallout) and are checked through the accretion and deposition rates they enter (cold_accretion.esm, ice_deposition.esm). Regime: supercell step 250 (t = 50 min), tile row j = 23, column i = 24: rain in layers 1-16 (up to 1.3e-2 kg/kg), snow in layers 6-33 and graupel in layers 1-33 (up to 1e-2), ice in layers 9-39, freezing level at layer 9, temperatures 199-298 K so n0sfac spans 1 to 7.5e3.

Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy single-column run (GNU real32 build, dt = 60 s, 59 layers, mp = 6, sfclay = 1, slab, YSU) at call 120 (step 60, 20:00 UTC) dumped by the instrumented fork and replayed through the real64 kernels/wsm6_driver; lowest 40 of the 59 layers (esm-spec 6.6 tests cannot rebind NLEV). Zero-condensate check for the precipitation distributions: qr = qs = qg = 0 throughout, so every inverse slope must equal exactly its 1/lambda_max value and n0sfac follows the temperature alone (1 in the warm lower layers, up to 42 aloft); only cloud ice is present (qi <= 5e-5 in layers 30-40), so the ice number concentration lies between its bounds there and at its floor 1e3 m^-3 below. Same reference chain and tolerance reasoning as the supercell test; the inverse-slope bounds are exact rational constants so their tolerance is 0, while lambda_s^-bvts at the bound carries the kernel's real32 rounding of bvts (0.4099999964 instead of 0.41: 4e-8 relative, 4e-10 absolute), hence abs 1e-9.
